source.author: verg
source.text: Nescia mens hominum fati sortisque futurae et servare modum, rebus sublata secundis!
source.text_original: Nescia mens hominum fati sortisque futurae / et servare modum, rebus sublata secundis!
source.text_english: The minds of men, ignorant of fate and of what is to come, and unable to keep to moderation when lifted up by success!

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Est enim magna afflictio generis humani, quia ut Poeta ait: Nescia mens hominum fati sortisque futurae, aliud sperat, aliudque evenit: de altero loco exspectat hostem, et alterius jaculo vulneratur.
reuse.text_original: Est enim magna afflictio generis humani, quia ut Poeta ait: Nescia mens hominum fati sortisque futurae, aliud sperat, aliudque evenit: de altero loco exspectat hostem, et alterius jaculo vulneratur.
reuse.text_english: For the affliction of the human race is great, because, as the Poet says: the mind of men is ignorant of fate and of the lot to come; it hopes for one thing and another happens. It expects an enemy from one place, and is wounded by a javelin from another.
